 Bailey Pemberton Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:13 AM PST 4 min read SGKN.SW +1.00% 
 SGKN 
 St. Galler Kantonalbank has quietly produced a strong share price story over the past few years, which naturally raises a question for anyone looking at the stock today. Are investors paying a price that is fully backed by the returns the bank earns on the capital it deploys into its business. 
 Over the past 5 years the share price has returned 98.4%, so the key issue is whether the bank's underlying return on capital can carry that kind of share performance. 
 The business model relies heavily on how efficiently it turns its balance sheet into earnings, which can shape long term expectations for return on equity, capital intensity and the timing of future cash flows. 
 If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why St. Galler Kantonalbank's 18.2x P/E tells a different valuation story . 
 The issue now is whether the returns St. Galler Kantonalbank earns on its capital are strong enough to make today's price look fully grounded in its underlying economics. 
 If you are weighing whether St. Galler Kantonalbank's 5 year return of 98.4% feels justified by the returns it earns on its capital, it can help to compare that pattern with 204 high quality undervalued stocks . 
 Does St. Galler Kantonalbank Look Fairly Valued on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns framework looks at how much profit St. Galler Kantonalbank earns on shareholder capital above its estimated cost. For this bank, the key inputs line up as a relatively measured, bank like pattern rather than an aggressive growth story. 
 Book Value sits at CHF521.32 per share, with a Stable Book Value assumption of CHF485.44 per share based on the median level over the past 5 years. Against that equity base, Stable EPS of CHF34.73 per share and an Average Return on Equity of 7.16% feed into the model. The Cost of Equity is set at CHF23.13 per share, which implies an Excess Return of CHF11.61 per share, so the bank is modeled as earning more than its required return but not by an extreme margin. 
 At a current share price of CHF709.00, the Excess Returns projections put St. Galler Kantonalbank's estimated intrinsic value broadly in line with the current share price. This suggests that the market price already reflects these moderate excess returns and steady balance sheet assumptions.
